name: PHYBench
intro: PHYBench 是由 178 名北京大学物理系学生参与构建的原创符号物理推理基准。题目先进入 Question Bank 并经过多轮专家审查，形成 757 题的 Reviewer’s Library；随后 81 名学生独立验证，其中 50 名为中国物理奥赛金牌得主，最终保留 500 题（66.1%）。o1 与 DeepSeek-R1 输出只作为专家审查的旁路辅助，不生成题目、答案或内部标注。评测先提取方框表达式，再分别计算符号等价准确率与分级表达式编辑距离分数。
org: School of Physics and Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Peking University; Beijing Computational Science Research Center
build_method: 178名学生人工出题, Question Bank多轮专家审查, 757题Reviewer’s Library, 81名学生独立验证后保留500题
metric: Symbolic-equivalence Accuracy, Expression Edit Distance (EED) Score, Human Baseline
eval_feature: 原创防污染题目, 方框答案提取, latex2sympy2_extended与SymPy等价检查, 扩展Zhang-Shasha表达式编辑距离, 人类基线
scale: 757题审稿人题库经81名学生、559份有效答卷筛选为500题；官方HF快照含100行完整题、400行仅题面数据与一份500行合并文件
build_method_en: 178 Student-authored Problems, Question Bank and Multi-round Expert Review, 757-item Reviewer's Library, Independent Validation by 81 Students Retaining 500
eval_feature_en: Original Contamination-resistant Problems, Boxed-answer Extraction, latex2sympy2_extended and SymPy Equivalence, Extended Zhang-Shasha Expression Edit Distance, Human Baseline
intro_en: PHYBench is an original symbolic physics reasoning benchmark built with contributions from 178 Peking University physics students. Questions enter the Question Bank and pass multi-round expert review before forming the 757-item Reviewer's Library; independent validation by 81 students, including 50 Chinese Physics Olympiad gold medalists, retains 500 questions (66.1 percent). o1 and DeepSeek-R1 outputs are only side inputs to expert review and never generate questions, answers, or internal annotations. Evaluation extracts a boxed expression, then separately reports exact symbolic-equivalence Accuracy and graded Expression Edit Distance.
scale_en: 757-item Reviewer's Library filtered to 500 questions by 81 students and 559 valid answer sheets; official HF snapshot has 100 full rows, 400 question-only rows, and one combined 500-row file
metric_en: Symbolic-equivalence Accuracy, Expression Edit Distance (EED) Score, Human Baseline

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-22; scope=source-stage academic-paper alignment for PHYBench; primary-paper-pin=https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16074v2 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.16074v2; paper-pdf-sha256=35cbf568e673839cb78212bb5a09d0f47690a8576954ebe4410f2d1f934d7e5d; official-code-pin=https://github.com/phybench-official/phybench/tree/d9db3ec7246f3678aaee65d44a32649ad93beea2; official-data-pin=https://huggingface.co/datasets/Eureka-Lab/PHYBench/tree/d6d91c787b7abb865eb2490a328bf85a9f5095f0. The official code is pinned to phybench-official/phybench commit d9db3ec7246f3678aaee65d44a32649ad93beea2 and the official dataset is pinned to Eureka-Lab/PHYBench revision d6d91c787b7abb865eb2490a328bf85a9f5095f0. Independently hashed code evidence is README 1f5adac71cdae213bbfbe376d06b8a3db060939596fe28f1f00bc8649376c68b, LICENSE 8d4f6779f96c77767b40ff51fc3b8123505e548718576772af7d5ec595c610dd, EED.py c3c689eb53cef8ce2933e51e64344ca628ad77b411d8f244a0062b06f2f62658, extended_zss implementation 781350903e70378e3bdd21b6db20f37edc3f7c624e58bb1f2e86f17fe6c61e0a, and latex_pre_process implementation 038780e8dbc619275e9ead4f020aa4e58abb378c70ae805c2dcd5ece782897eb. Independently hashed data evidence is the HF README e306cc446a9ecb490041766c3b3ed4f3e6e51428dfad98e0c894d4079bb95b37, 100-row full-question file a01955ffb2ff86d7833770d3d9f308e3bc1b0e2fea92c5092c4e68a619048a6b, 400-row question-only file 599c0f7055bf7a58a2b8f80a8915e726086ecdc7650c369b963aaafb4ac08c18, and combined 500-row file 912b17db6a4fef6f6bc12bc2321a9e8d9e919392ce78ae1629b5b0a76f7cf42d. The construction topology follows the paper rather than the previous flattened serial sketch. A total of 178 Peking University physics students author and curate original or substantially adapted problems, with symbolic formula or expression answers, self-contained wording, explicit variables and assumptions, one checkable interpretation, broad coverage across six physics domains, and difficulty ranging from high school through undergraduate work to Physics Olympiad level. Drafts enter the internal Question Bank with questions, reference answers, worked solutions, contributor information, and revision feedback. Multi-round expert review checks physical correctness, solvability, wording, and unique interpretation; it revises or rejects deficient drafts. The 757 count belongs after this Question Bank and expert-review stage: it is the Reviewer's Library sent to human validation, not the raw number before expert review. Outputs from o1 and DeepSeek-R1 are a dashed side input only to expert review, used to reveal ambiguity or unintended interpretations; they never create questions, reference answers, solutions, ground truth, or internal annotations and therefore are not a serial construction stage. Independent validation uses 81 students, 50 of whom are Chinese Physics Olympiad gold medalists. Each student receives eight questions; the study records 559 valid answer sheets. Review flags and disagreements are resolved, and 500 of the 757 questions are retained, a 66.1 percent retention rate. The finalized benchmark is text-only and spans six domains. The evaluation topology is also split explicitly. The unified zero-shot instruction asks for step-by-step reasoning and a final boxed LaTeX expression. API experiments use provider defaults where the paper says so; documented local inference uses temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, and max_new_tokens 32768. Evaluation first locates and extracts the final boxed expression, strips wrappers and formatting noise, and handles missing or unparseable answers. Expressions are normalized with latex2sympy2_extended and SymPy simplify or equality checks. Exact Accuracy is a binary branch: a symbolically equivalent prediction scores 100 and a non-equivalent, invalid, or absent prediction scores zero before dataset averaging. EED is a separate graded branch rather than a fallback synonym for Accuracy. Prediction and reference formulas become ordered expression trees; the implementation applies an extended Zhang-Shasha tree edit distance. For an edit of size x, cost is min(x, 0.6*(x-5)+5): cost is unchanged through five nodes and only marginal cost beyond five nodes is charged at 60 percent. With r equal to edit distance divided by ground-truth tree size, EED is 100 when r equals zero, 60 minus 100r when zero is less than r and r is less than 0.6, and zero when r is at least 0.6. The two scores remain separately reported. The paper reports that EED yields 204 percent more sample efficiency than binary Accuracy for ranking comparisons. Human results are also a distinct evidence branch: from 559 valid answer sheets, human Accuracy is 61.9 plus or minus 2.1 percent and human EED is 70.4 plus or minus 1.8, with 10,000 bootstrap resamples. The release boundary is preserved rather than inferred away. The pinned HF data contains 100 complete records with question, answer, and solution, plus 400 question-only records; the combined file contains exactly 500 records. Loading all three packaged files in the HF viewer yields 1000 rows because the combined file duplicates the two subsets, not because PHYBench contains 1000 unique questions. HF metadata declares MIT. The pinned Git repository also carries MIT but has no tagged release. Its public code implements the EED path and EED-specific parsing or rejection behavior only; it does not provide a complete model-inference runner, the paper's full boxed-answer extraction pipeline, or the full symbolic-Accuracy runner. Accordingly the diagrams use primary edges for human construction, validation, and the two metric branches, while fixed evidence, o1/R1 review assistance, the pinned data snapshot, and the released-code subset are dashed secondary edges. This note does not infer unshipped implementation from the paper and does not treat generated assets or dataset viewer row counts as proof of final methodological signoff. Formal publication evidence [site-a12c-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 1885×1026 (English) and 1892×1025 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 1883×1024 and 1890×1023. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
